subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin memorySearch.extraPaths accept arbitrary JSONL logs, or should raw message logs stay outside builtin memory and use sessionMemory, QMD, or a converter/plugin workflow?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but accepting arbitrary JSONL raw logs changes the memory product boundary and security/privacy exposure rather than being a strict bug fix.

options.title: Document non-builtin workflow
options.body: Keep builtin extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only for now, document the supported sessionMemory/QMD/converter-plugin path for raw logs, and close this only after that explicit decision is posted.

options.title: Sponsor native JSONL support
options.body: Approve a scoped native JSONL design that covers schema detection, per-line chunking, line mapping, memory_get behavior, watcher filtering, docs, tests, and security review.

options.title: Design a plugin/API extension first
options.body: If current plugin surfaces cannot support the converter or memory-plugin route cleanly, open a narrower plugin API design item before changing builtin ingestion.

recommendation.title: Document non-builtin workflow
recommendation.body: Keep builtin extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only for now, document the supported sessionMemory/QMD/converter-plugin path for raw logs, and close this only after that explicit decision is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already left the clearest maintainer-side review on this item and is tied to the historical memory host boundary being evaluated.
